teaser.text: Target Corporation is a U.S. retailer that sells everyday necessities and more style-led goods through stores and digital channels. It earns most of its money from merchandise, then adds income from advertising, marketplace commissions, memberships, partners and a credit-card arrangement.

stock.title: Target stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Target's stock forecast maps bear, base and bull scenarios, then tests the recovery against traffic, cash generation and valuation.
stock.opening: Target's weighted forecast is $151.19 in October 2029, after $133.73 in October 2027. It hinges on traffic, comparable sales, margins without tariff refunds and cash generation improving.
stock.closing: The full memo also answers how Target's business works, how it compares with rivals, how management is executing, and where its risks lie.

blocks.heading: Where could Target's shares be in October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted price is $133.73 in October 2027. That is a 10% loss including dividends. The final weighted price is $151.19 in October 2029. That is a 7% gain including dividends. The bear case has 28% probability, and the base case has 55%. The bull case has 17%.

blocks.heading: What has to go right or wrong for Target?

paragraphs.text: The base case assumes revenue of $111,000 million in October 2027, followed by 2% annual growth. Margins rise from 3.7% to 3.8% and then 3.9%, producing earnings of $4,107 million, $4,302.36 million, and $4,503.915 million. Q2 traffic rose 3.6%, comparable sales rose 3.8%, and all six core categories grew, supporting a measured recovery.

The bear case holds revenue near $108,000 million before falling to $106,000 million, with margins between 2.8% and 3.0%. It reflects weaker discretionary demand, markdowns, and a fading traffic rebound. The bull case grows revenue from $112,000 million to $121,139.2 million and margins from 4.0% to 4.4%, requiring store resets, better assortment, and productive digital investment.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Target today?

paragraphs.text: The P/E ratio translates the price into a claim on earnings. It divides the share price by earnings per share, so a 16.0x P/E means investors pay sixteen dollars for each dollar of annual earnings. If Target earns $10 per share and the stock trades at $160, the P/E is 16.0x. But the denominator can be temporarily inflated when an unusual benefit, such as the tariff refund recognized in Q2 2026, raises reported profit.

dividend.opening: Target’s dividend starts at $4.68 per share. Cash coverage has varied: payouts exceeded free cash flow in some years, while Target prioritizes profitable growth, then dividends, then buybacks.
dividend.closing: The full memo also explains Target’s business, rivals, management choices and risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Target pay per share?

paragraphs.text: The dividend starts at $4.68 per share. The base case applies 3% annual increases, reaching $4.82 and $4.97. The bear case freezes the dividend, while the bull case applies 8% increases, reaching $5.05 and $5.45. The five-year record shows uninterrupted increases, but investment needs and volatile cash flow limit confidence in faster growth.

blocks.heading: Is Target’s dividend covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Revenue declined across the latest three fiscal years, while operating margin recovered from its fiscal 2022 low. Target’s real free cash flow margin moved from negative in fiscal 2022 to positive in the latest two years, but inventory and supplier-payment timing can make a single year misleading. Diluted EPS recovered from the fiscal 2022 trough; real free cash flow per share shows cash after investment and stock-based pay, while buybacks can lift per-share results and payouts exceeded free cash flow in some years.

The record also shows why free cash flow is not an absolute legal limit on dividends or buybacks. A company can use cash already held or borrow when current free cash flow is negative, but that reduces its cushion or increases debt. Target says it invests first in profitable growth, pays a competitive dividend second, and uses excess cash for buybacks last. In the first six months of 2026, it made no share repurchases while continuing to pay dividends. A buyback authorization is permission, not a promise.

blocks.heading: What should I watch in Target's next results?

paragraphs.text: At the next Q3 call, investors should ask whether store resets and Beauty Studio are increasing traffic and turning visits into purchases. Home and apparel still need work, and a merchandise reset may take time to show up in sales. The sharper test is whether new products sell before markdowns and whether stores remain in stock.

Finally, shareholder litigation over ESG disclosures and an open federal tax audit covering 2021–2024 could affect cash or earnings, though no likely amount is established. The complete test is simple: can Target’s stores and digital channels produce enough recurring cash to fund investment, dividends and debt while the temporary refund disappears?
